_commissioner_comment: Runs the engine. Trades involving him are labelled in Section 10; the trade finder publishes all six pairs automatically (decided 2026-10-06).

yahoo._historical_league_keys_comment: Corrected Sep 2026. Eight of the nine were wrong, and had been since the first commit -- config said 380.l.23647 for 2017-18 where Yahoo's own team keys say 375.l.132631. The values here are derived from the league prefix of the team keys in data/historical/all_teams.json and RECORDS.team_name_history, which came from Yahoo pulls and agree with each other for every season; the game ids then form the real NBA sequence 375/385/395/402/410/418/428/454/466. verify_project_integrity re-checks this on every run.

league_structure._add_budget_comment: New for 2026-27: each team gets 3 adds per FANTASY week (week 7, 14 days, has one budget), covering both the Monday window (12:01 AM on the fantasy week's first day until five minutes before the last NBA game of that night starts -- agreed in the group chat, Nick 10-28) and mid-week adds posted in the group chat, which take effect the following Monday. There was NO add budget before 2026-27, so historical add counts are not violations of it. Trades do not cost an add: sync_transactions records both sides of a trade as an add, and those are marked '(via trade)' and excluded.
league_structure._rounds_comment: total_rounds = roster_size - il_slots and is fixed: you draft into every roster spot that is not an IL slot. keepers_per_team and total_draft_rounds describe the CURRENT season ONLY, and are meaningful only while every manager keeps the same number. From 2027-28 keeper counts differ by manager -- see keeper_rules and data_loader.keepers_for().
league_structure._time_zone_comment: The league's clock (Nick, 10-30): 'whatever time it is in Portland, Oregon, that is always going to be the league's clock', daylight saving included. An IANA zone name, never a fixed offset. Every league day, Monday window and fantasy-week boundary is in this time; every date taken from 'now' or from a Yahoo timestamp goes through modules/league_clock.py. Required: missing raises. claude/LEAGUE_RULES.md rule 0.

tiebreaker_rules._comment: Every tie the rules can produce, named. Anything not listed here RAISES -- code never guesses a tiebreak (Nick, 10-07). standings/fallback: regular-season standings, also the draft order and playoff seeding.
tiebreaker_rules._regular_season_week: A tied regular-season week is a T in the standings for both managers; nobody wins it. This follows Yahoo, which is how the league settles it (Nick, 10-20). Separate from series_week and cup_game on purpose.
tiebreaker_rules._tie_win_value: A T counts as this many wins for standings position: winning percentage is (W + 0.5*T) / (W + L + T), Yahoo's formula. A season series can end tied (e.g. 2-2-1); then head-to-head cannot separate the two and total points does.
tiebreaker_rules._series_week: A tied week inside a best-of-3 playoff series: the higher seed takes the week.
tiebreaker_rules._cup_game: A tied single game in the Cup: the higher (Cup) seed advances.
tiebreaker_rules._cup_seeding: Cup seeding tied on total points: the better regular-season finish gets the higher seed.

pre_data_era._note: The two seasons played before the current rules. Deliberately excluded from all_standings and RECORDS, deliberately still counted in the honour roll, so these are added to the nine-season derived totals to reconcile against LEAGUEHISTORY.xlsx. Key names match that file's columns exactly: titles_won is the regular season, playoff_championships is the bracket. They were previously named first_place_finishes and titles, where 'titles' meant playoff championships -- the opposite of what titles_won means one file over.

season._season_number_comment: Two counts, two scopes -- the same 11-vs-9 split as career honours. data_era_season_number: seasons with Yahoo data, 2017-18 on (this is the 10th); 'all-time' in the newsletter means this era. league_season_number: the whole league, counting 2014-15 and 2015-16 (records only, no stats; 2016-17 was not played) -- this is the 12th. Every consumer picks one explicitly; there is no plain season_number.

nba_unscheduled_window._comment: Required (modules/nba_schedule.py, task 46). The NBA posts each team's last games of the regular season only after the NBA Cup group stage (11-27): until then the schedule has {games_per_team} minus 2 per team and nothing from {from} to {to}, the knockout window. The loader adds a stand-in (tbd) for every owed game, paired with another team that owes one, spread over these days; it never writes them to the schedule file. from/to/cup_final null = no window, and any team short of games_per_team raises. A team over games_per_team raises; stand-ins still needed on or after from raise (the NBA has posted them: refetch). cup_final: the Cup final is not a regular-season game; basketball-reference lists it (marked NBA Cup), so the refetch drops the one NBA Cup game on this day. Lives in season beside nba_schedule_file because it describes that file: update both at the season reset.
nba_unscheduled_window.source: NBA key dates, Emirates NBA Cup 2026 knockout rounds (quarterfinals Dec 4-5, semifinals Dec 8-9, final Dec 11)

season._legacy_advice_comment: Section 10's old C2/C3 advice (waiver plans and the trade finder). "off": the weekly build does not run it at all (about 15 minutes saved) and Section 10 prints one line where it went, "The advice returns with the new engine." "on": as before. Required: missing or any other value raises. Nick, 11-01: the old advice won't publish; it is being rebuilt as advice v2 (claude/ADVICE_V2_DESIGN.md). The modules stay: v2's replay check may reuse pieces.
season._advice_comment: C2/C3 (Section 10 waiver plans and trade finder) publish from this report week when the premise check (scripts/validate_marginal_value.py) is CLEAR for this season, or when advice_premise_override names the band the check recorded. Otherwise they run as a preview (output/advice_preview_weekN.html) and Section 10 says why. UNSTABLE, a missing check or another season's check always block. MARGINAL means talk, not ship -- unless Nick overrides it here, dated and attributed.

advice_premise_override.reason: Nick, 10-29: ship Section 10 in week 3; do our best.

season._advice_premise_override_comment: Nick, 10-29, after the premise gate came back FAIL (gap points 78.7 vs 169 needed, mutual-gain swaps 22 vs 24; C2C3_GATE_RESULT_2026-10-29): publish Section 10 anyway. The gate keeps running and recording; every build prints 'published on Nick's override of a FAIL premise gate (10-29)'. Remove this key to return to CLEAR-only.
season._stream_drop_pool_comment: Nick, 10-29: a one-week stream (Section 10's this-week plan) may only drop one of the bottom N ACTIVE players on the roster by PROJECTED points per game (the PLAYERLIST pre-season projection, not actual-blended). No keeper protection: a projected keeper in the bottom N is on the block. IL occupants are not ranked (dropping one frees no active spot for the add); a player with no projection is never a drop. Fixed from the roster at the start of the plan; players the plan adds never join it. Season moves are not limited by it. Required: missing or below 1 raises (STREAM_DROPS_RESULT_2026-10-29).

presentation._magic_number_comment: No magic number reaches the drafter or the page before this report week: not the ANGLES ranking (no CLINCH WATCH), the storyline alerts, the standing threads, Section 7's facts, or any template. It is still computed and kept in the report JSON (power_rankings[].magic_number); clinch logic is unchanged. Required: missing or not a whole number >= 1 raises. Nick, 11-02: "we probably should have just no mention at all of 'magic numbers' until like, at least week 8 or something? Theyre pretty pointless to report on before that point."

season_structure._comment: Per-season week layout. season.regular_season_weeks describes ONLY the current season; historical seasons varied and the engine must not assume one shape for all time. regular_through = last regular-season week. bracket = a postseason bracket was played.
season_structure._pre_yahoo: 2014-15 and 2015-16 predate usable Yahoo data and have no matchup records; their results live only in LEAGUEHISTORY.xlsx to-date totals. The league took 2016-17 off entirely.

2019-20.note: COVID stoppage; season ended wk19 with no bracket played

2020-21.note: 18-week season after the bubble; bracket in wks 17-18

2021-22.note: 22-week season (All-Star double week); bracket in wks 21-22

2026-27.note: new format: best-of-3 series wks 16-21 (semis 16-18, final and 3rd-place 19-21), cup wks 22-23

season_structure._derivation: THROUGH 2025-26 ONLY: the bracket was always the last two fantasy weeks, so regular_through = last_week - 2 whenever a bracket was played. The last week is not a fixed number because Yahoo stretches any week containing the All-Star break to 14 days, which changes how many fantasy weeks a season fits into; 2021-22 ran 22 weeks, not 23, so its bracket was weeks 21-22 and its regular season ended at week 20. That rule does NOT hold from 2026-27 onward -- see postseason_format, where the postseason is eight weeks long.

postseason_format._comment: The league format in force from effective_from onward. Earlier seasons played a two-week, single-game bracket in the final two weeks and are described individually in season_structure. All week ranges are inclusive [first, last].
postseason_format.name: three_stage

regular_season.title: League Champion
regular_season.decides: final standings, draft order, and payouts
regular_season.note: 5 meetings per opponent is deliberately odd so no season series can end drawn. 3 opponents x 5 = 15 weeks.

playoffs.title: Playoff Champion
playoffs.note: Every week of a series is played even after the series is decided, so a 2-0 series still plays its third week. The series winner is whoever wins the most of the three weeks.

cup.title: Cup Champion

rounds.name: Cup Third Place
rounds.note: Played and recorded for the stat history. Carries no stake (payouts.cup_third_place).

cup.prize: an extra (6th) keeper for the following season
cup.note: Single games, not series. The 2026-27 Cup is the first one ever played; its winner sets the 2027-28 keeper asymmetry.

simulations._season_sims: Simulations for every season-long simulator: title odds, playoff odds, Cup odds. ONE number on purpose (Nick, 10-20: don't split): the bracket simulators read the same keyed week matrices as title odds. Raised from 10,000 on 2026-10-21 (Nick): once untagged absences were simulated, 10,000 sims moved title odds up to 0.6 points between seeds; 50,000 holds them to about 0.3 and costs about 30 seconds.
simulations._marginal_value_sims: marginal_value (waiver, trade and keeper advice). Absences are persistent blocks, so one valuation's standard error at 400 sims was 15-20 points against C2's 10-point floor; at 3,000 a season-long add's is about 3.7. See claude/BASELINE_INJURY_RESULT_2026-10-21.md.
simulations._premise_trade_sample: scripts/validate_marginal_value.py samples this many one-for-one swaps per sample, in this many disjoint samples, instead of all 1,350 from both sides (25 minutes at 3,000 sims). The band must agree across samples or the gate records UNSTABLE (Nick, 10-21).
simulations._marginal_value_shortlist_sims: The advice pre-filter: every candidate is scored at this count and only the shortlist reaches marginal_value_sims. At 40 its noise was about 30 points -- a good add could be cut before the precise check ever saw it (Nick, 10-21). 200 costs about 45 s a weekly build.

projection_shrinkage._k0_games: How much a player's season-to-date FPPG counts against his projection: weight on actuals = k / (k + k0_games), k = games he has actually played this season (modules/projections.py, PlayerProjection.effective_fppg). One curve, no threshold; the projection never drops to zero weight. 20 set 2026-10-28 (HANDOFF_SHRINKAGE_CURVE): measured k0 is 4.7 against the league mean (589 player-seasons), 13 against prior-season FPPG (401), 24.5 against the real Yahoo projection (21 players); the better the prior, the larger k0, and 20 is the safer end. Replaced MIN_GAMES_FOR_ACTUAL = 10 (pure actuals from 10 games), which was chosen, not measured.

projection_error._scale: Persistent error in a player's level -- the engine being wrong about who is good, all season (modules/projections.py, projection_error_sd). Its width is DERIVED, not chosen: in the normal model behind the shrinkage curve, k0 = (per-game sd / prior error)^2, so the error at zero games is DEFAULT_PLAYER_VARIANCE / sqrt(projection_shrinkage.k0_games) = 0.35 / sqrt(20) = 7.8% of his level, narrowing to that times sqrt(k0 / (k + k0)) after k appearances. This key scales that derived value; 1.0 = as derived. Change k0 and the width follows. Set 2026-10-28 (HANDOFF_PERSISTENT_ERROR).

roster_moves._yahoo_max_adds_comment: What Yahoo's Max Adds per week must show (Nick set it 10-31). It differs from league_structure.weekly_add_budget (3, the league's rule) ON PURPOSE: Yahoo sees a group-chat claim only when it is applied in the NEXT week's window (rule 7), so in one Yahoo week a team can apply up to 3 claims from the week before plus 3 adds of its own. The engine enforces the 3; the settings-drift check (modules/yahoo_settings.py) requires Yahoo to show this. Required: missing raises.
roster_moves._ledger_mode: The move ledger (step 2, modules/move_ledger.py; claude/SELF_RUNNING_DESIGN.md s.6): "shadow" or "on", required (missing or anything else raises). shadow (Nick, 11-04: the first real window, 11-09, runs beside the hand-written claim_week rulings): the ledger records group-chat moves, checks them, publishes the Monday checklist and verifies the window against Yahoo, but every add count still comes from TRANSACTION_RULINGS and nothing is priced from a pending move; the nightly run reports where the ledger's counts differ. on: the ledger's claim weeks are the add counts (transaction_rulings.add_budget_week takes the ledger) and the roster plan treats a pending move as a known pickup from its window. Nick switches it after a clean window. SWITCHED TO on (Nick, 2026-11-10) after the clean 11-09 window: all 6 week-3 claims applied, 0 shadow differences; the week-3 claim_week rulings stay and agree with the ledger. From week 4 on, no hand-written claim_week rulings for chat claims.
roster_moves._ledger_verify_from: Yahoo transactions on or after this league day that fall outside a Monday window and match no ledger entry are flagged (rule 4; move_ledger.verify). The day after the last window run without the ledger (11-02); earlier moves were settled by hand.
roster_moves._il_eligible_tags: Only these Yahoo tags make a player eligible for an IL slot (LEAGUE_RULES.md, 2026-27 IL rules, rule 2). The simulator's roster plan treats a player with a live INJURY_OVERRIDES entry as O (modules/roster_plan.py).
roster_moves._longrun_sims: The long-run value's simulations (modules/roster_plan.py LongRun): the roster plan's activation drop (who goes when an IL return makes 16 active), the plan's mid-week-return choice, and advice's long-run measure (advice_v2.Settings.long_sims reads this key, so the plan and advice keep one measure). 200 (Nick, 11-12, task 44b s.1): at advice's old 16 the choice among near-tied players depended on the seed (44a s.6.1: Garrett's week-8 drop was Fox, Camara or Sarr by seed). Required: missing raises.
roster_moves._activation_tie_band: The tie band, in standard errors of the paired difference (the same draws for both rosters): two candidates whose long-run losses differ by at most this many SEs are TIED, and the tie goes to the lower projection, then the name (the rule before 44a); a mid-week returner is activated early only when that beats waiting by more than the band (ties keep him in IL). 2.0 (Nick, 11-12, task 44b s.1). Required: missing raises.
roster_moves._replacement_rank: The level of every pickup the roster plan makes (modules/roster_plan.py): an IL placement or an empty active spot, at each fantasy-week window, up to weekly_add_budget. Not a named player but a stand-in, 'Replacement for <player> (level)' or 'Replacement for open spot N, <manager> (level)', at the replacement_rank-th best effective_fppg among free agents as the window opens (before that window's drops, so pickup order cannot matter; the league has no waivers). An IL stand-in carries the injured player's positions and NBA team; an open-spot stand-in, the rank-th free agent's. 4 (Nick, 10-28: 'something like the 3rd-5th best'; real pickups weigh FPPG and schedule fit, not best producer). When the real pickup syncs, he replaces the stand-in.

injured_drop._comment: When the roster plan drops an injured player instead of holding him in an active spot (task 18b; claude/INJURED_DROP_DESIGN.md s.3; modules/injured_drop.py, called by modules/roster_plan.py at every future window). Stake units are the change in rs_weight x P(regular-season title) + playoff_weight x P(champion); a point in week w is worth that week's stake x the density at zero of the team's simulated margin (output/stakes.json, the previous run's). Drop only when holding costs at least (1 + margin) x dropping AND the difference is at least floor. M, F and K were fitted 11-04 on Nick's scenarios (s.5) as revised by him that day (claude/HANDOFF_18B_REFIT_AND_WIRE_2026-11-04.md: 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9 pinned; 1, 7, 9b, 10, 11 direction only), on six simulation seeds; the region common to all six is M 0-1.10, K 0-0.36, F 0-0.122, and the values are its deepest point, rounded (tests/injured_drop_scenarios.py, scripts/fit_injured_drop.py; claude/INJURED_DROP_RESULT_2_2026-11-04.md). RE-FIT 11-12 with the causal price of a point (stakes schema 3, claude/CAUSAL_LEVERAGE_RESULT_2026-11-12.md): the scenarios' toy season draws every week independently, so its leverage was already causal (near-tie / all-iteration 0.97 over 493 toy team-weeks; tests/test_injured_drop.py pins it); the fit is unchanged -- the same region and deepest point on all six seeds -- and M, F and K stand. The LIVE costs were the ones on the inflated scale (about 1.4-1.5x); the causal stakes fix them. Every key is required: missing raises.
injured_drop._rs_weight: Nick, 11-03: the regular-season title against the playoff title, 2 to 1, as the money ($180 v $90). Sets the stake of every scenario.
injured_drop._playoff_weight: The 1 of Nick's 2 to 1 (11-03). Sets the stake of every scenario; the playoff weeks decide scenarios 4, 8 and 10.
injured_drop._rs_little_left: Before the playoffs a team with a regular-season title chance under this has little left to play for and holds every keeper candidate (Nick, 11-03). Scenario 6 (and 7 and 11b's teams are under it).
injured_drop._playoff_little_left: From the playoffs on, the same with the playoff title chance (Nick's revision, 11-03: one or the other, never both; every team makes the playoffs, so an 0-10 team's playoff chance must not count before week 16). No scenario is under it.
injured_drop._protected_keepers: A team's top 4 by keep chance (K = 5) are never dropped (Nick, 11-01; ADVICE_V2_DESIGN decision 3a). Scenario 8: a 55-FPPG player is a top-4 keeper in practice (Nick, 11-04).
injured_drop._keeper_candidates: A keeper candidate is in his team's top 6 by keep chance (Nick agreed, 11-03): he carries the keeper term, and a team with little left to play for holds him. Scenarios 1, 6 and 9.
injured_drop._margin: M. Drops need holding to cost at least 1.25 x dropping. The drops pinned in scenarios 3 (the binding one: holding costs about 2.15 x dropping) and 9 cap it at about 1.1; nothing pinned needs it above 0 -- it is inertia by design (s.3.4: a drop is permanent, the stakes are estimates, small edges flip the nightly odds). Fitted value, the common region's deepest point.
injured_drop._floor: F, stake units. The edge must be at least this. Scenario 3 and 9's pinned drops cap it at about 0.12; scenarios 7 and 10 sit near it (7 holds, its edge about 0.033; 10 drops, about 0.049 -- both direction-only). Fitted value.
injured_drop._keeper_weight: K, stake units per unit of keep chance, for a keeper candidate. Scenario 9's pinned drop of a no. 5 candidate caps it at about 0.36 (at M = 0); scenario 1's direction check needs only K >= 0. At 0.075 the no. 5 in scenario 1 still drops (claude/INJURED_DROP_RESULT_2_2026-11-04.md). Fitted value.

stakes._comment: The causal leverage in output/stakes.json (schema 3; modules/title_odds_run, claude/HANDOFF_CAUSAL_LEVERAGE_2026-11-12.md s.1): per team and week, P(title | wins w) - P(title | loses w) among the season pass's NEAR-TIE iterations (|margin| < near_tie_band), so a week's win carries what the week causes and not the season-long luck of the iterations that win it. injured_drop.point_value -- the one price of a point (18b and the advice's title term) -- uses it. Every key is required: missing raises.
stakes._near_tie_band: Points. Chosen 11-12 from {25, 50, 75} on the 8 development team-weeks of the direct check (+40 points to one team in one week, same draws, against causal leverage x density x 40; _to_delete/leverage/teamweeks.json): full/predicted median 0.97 (range 0.93-1.02) at 25, 0.95 (0.84-0.97) at 50, 0.90 (0.80-1.02) at 75; the all-iteration leverage 0.64 (0.56-0.74). Wider bands keep more of the season-long luck. claude/CAUSAL_LEVERAGE_RESULT_2026-11-12.md.
stakes._near_tie_wider: When fewer than near_tie_min iterations win (or lose) within the band, the band widens to the next of these, recorded in the row's causal_why. Beyond the last, the causal leverage is null (worth 0 per point, recorded) -- never the all-iteration leverage.
stakes._near_tie_min: Iterations per side. At 300 a side the bootstrap SE is about 0.04 on a leverage near 0.2; on the 11-11 pass every team-week had 784-2,221 a side within 25 points.
stakes._causal_bootstrap: Resamples behind each row's causal_se, seeded from the pass's seed, the team and the week (deterministic; nothing drawn from the pass).

durability_prior._comment: WHERE THE BASELINE HAZARD GETS player_proj_GP, and deliberately NOT the live data/PLAYERLIST.xlsx. The column changes meaning when the season starts: PRE-SEASON it is projected games out of 82 with a durability haircut on everyone (measured 2026-10-22 across all three stored snapshots: mean 69.1-69.3, sd 4.9-5.0, 31% of players within one game of the median), IN-SEASON it is games out of those REMAINING, marked down only for players Yahoo already knows are hurt (a fresh fetch the same day: mean 77.7, sd 2.74, 96% within one game of the median; GP correlates 0.52 against the stored file while FPPG correlates 0.97 -- only GP breaks). Taking it live in-season drops the hazard from about 16% to about 1.5% a game, which switches the injury model off and puts title odds back to Hayden at 78% (claude/HANDOFF_DURABILITY_PRIOR_2026-10-22.md).
durability_prior._which: The NEWEST PRE-SEASON snapshot, named here rather than inferred from a directory listing, so the prior cannot change under a run that did not ask it to. Scoring inputs (projectedFPPG, total projected FP) still come live from data/PLAYERLIST.xlsx -- those refresh correctly.
durability_prior._next_season: A new season sets this once, in the preseason checklist, to that season's first snapshot: take a PLAYERLIST before week 1 (py scripts/check_playerlist.py --snapshot) and point this key at it. verify_project_integrity FAILS when the file is missing, or when its GP column has lost its pre-season dispersion, or when it was taken after the season's first week started. PRESEASON_2026-27.md and SEASON_RESET.md say so.
durability_prior._flat_gp_share_max: Refuse a GP column with more than this share of players within one game of the median -- that is the in-season shape (96% today) rather than the pre-season one (31%). Used by scripts/check_playerlist.py and by the prior loader itself.

absence_chain._comment: Yahoo injury designations that drive the absence chain (modules/absence.py): P(he plays game k of his team's games from the tag's anchor | he missed every earlier one), for k = 1, 2, 3. The 2026-27 vocabulary is P, Q, D, O, OFS. P is healthy, OFS is a season-long out carried by absence_baseline (projected GP 0), and these three drive the chain.
absence_chain._stated: NICK'S STATED JUDGEMENT, NOT MEASURED. O and Q approved 2026-10-19 (as O and GTD, before Yahoo renamed GTD to Q); D added 2026-10-22, between Q and O at every game. Q's second game is deliberately LOWER than its first: a questionable player who then actually sat is in worse shape than the tag said.
absence_chain._calibration: Do not guess these from the historical log. It records is_injured, not the tag that was showing, and the tags it would have carried are the retired GTD/DTD vocabulary -- so measuring Q and D from it needs an assumption about how the old names map onto the new ones. That is a judgement for Nick, not a measurement (claude/HANDOFF_YAHOO_TAGS_2026-10-22.md sec.5).

absence_baseline._comment: Untagged absences (modules/absence.py, the baseline hazard). Every player misses games he is not tagged for: Yahoo's player_proj_GP is his projected GP over his team's REMAINING games, so his per-game miss rate is (remaining team games - projected GP) / remaining team games. Those misses come in BLOCKS, persistent within a simulated season: an absence is short (mostly one-game rests) or long (a real injury), chosen per absence; a healthy spell between absences is memoryless. The rate is not a parameter -- it is the projection. Only the block SHAPE lives here.
absence_baseline._nba_games_per_team: The NBA regular season. The schedule file lists 80 per team: the last 2 are set by the NBA Cup group stage and are added later. Yahoo projects GP over all 82, so the unscheduled games count as remaining when the rate is taken.
absence_baseline._measured: Fitted 2026-10-21 by maximum likelihood to every absence run in HISTORICAL_PLAYERLOG 2017-18..2025-26 (a team game with zero fantasy points while rostered; 2,805 complete runs plus 375 runs cut off by a roster move, treated as at-least-that-long). Two geometric components: 75% of absences average 1.24 games, 25% average 9.5. Mean absence 3.3 games. Re-fit with the same procedure; do not hand-tune these to hit the calibration bands.

keeper_rules._comment: Keeper counts are per-season and need NOT be uniform across managers. A manager's live picks = league_structure.total_rounds minus their keeper count, and keepers always occupy the LAST rounds. Any season after the last one listed in `seasons` inherits `default`.

2026-27.note: The last uniform year. Everyone keeps 6 (rounds 10-15) and drafts rounds 1-9, 36 live picks in all. No Cup had been played yet when these keepers were chosen.

default.note: The previous season's Cup winner keeps 6 (rounds 10-15) and drafts rounds 1-9; the other three keep 5 (rounds 11-15) and draft rounds 1-10. 39 live + 21 keeper = 60 = 15 rounds x 4 teams, so round 10 holds three picks rather than four.

cup_winners._comment: Season -> the manager who won that season's Cup (weeks 22-23). That manager keeps one extra player the FOLLOWING season. null means the Cup has not been played or the result has not been recorded yet; keepers_for() refuses to guess and treats every manager as base until it is filled in. scripts/start_new_season.py will not let a season be archived while its Cup winner is still null.

yahoo_settings._comment: The Yahoo league settings the engine models, beyond league_structure and roster_moves (step 1a, 10-31): the settings-drift check (modules/yahoo_settings.py, scripts/check_yahoo_settings.py) refuses when Yahoo shows anything else. Read from Yahoo 10-31 and put to Nick the same day (step 1a); his answer is recorded in claude/STEP1A_RESULT_2026-10-31.md. Settings the engine has no rule for are listed in _unchecked, on purpose. Every key is required: missing raises.
yahoo_settings._uses_playoff_comment: Yahoo's own playoffs stay off: the league's postseason (weeks 16-23, then the Cup) is the engine's (postseason_format).
yahoo_settings._waivers_comment: Rule 8: no waivers, free agents first come first served.
yahoo_settings._trade_deadline_comment: Yahoo trade_end_date. Nick confirmed 10-31 that 2027-03-04 is the league's real deadline; the move ledger (step 2) refuses a chat trade after it.
yahoo_settings._stat_values_comment: Yahoo's fantasy-point value of each scoring category. The engine takes points from Yahoo, so a changed value would silently make this season's points incomparable with history.

hub._comment: The hub page (Step 1b, claude/HANDOFF_STEP1B_HUB_PAGE_2026-10-31.md; modules/hub_state.py). Every key required (stash_top_n added 11-05). free_agents_top_n: how many free agents the hub lists, by Yahoo projection. light_night_max: a day on the games grid with this many players or fewer playing is marked light (the approved mockup's legend: 4 or fewer).
hub._stash_top_n: Task 42 (Nick, 11-05): the hub's stash table under the free agents lists at most this many free agents tagged O or OFS (rule 2: only they can go straight into an IL slot), by Yahoo's projection. A display, not advice. Required: missing or below 1 raises (modules/hub_state.hub_config).
hub._matchup_framing: Task 48a (Nick, 11-10; starting values for Nick to tune): how the hub's nightly matchup paragraph picks its framing, first match wins: Final (every day banked); Blowout (the leader's win % >= blowout_win_pct); Comeback (the team below comeback_close_below % at the closing line is now at comeback_now_at % or more, or a team that was below comeback_rise_was_below % at the previous priced run rose comeback_rise_points points or more since it -- Nick, 11-10: a favourite growing its lead is no comeback, and the team that trailed at the close and leads now stays a comeback all week); Lead change (the banked leader differs from the previous priced run's); Close (both teams between close_low and close_high %); Steady otherwise. Percent points. Required: missing or malformed raises (modules/hub_matchups.framing_config).

advice._comment: Advice v2 (claude/HANDOFF_ADVICE_V2_2026-11-11.md; modules/advice_live.py). Every key required: missing or anything else raises (advice_live.hub_switch).
advice._hub: "off" or "on". Whether the hub shows the advice view (an "Advice" link beside "Trade block" and one card per manager). The engine computes and stores the advice either way (output/advice_latest.json, output/advice_history.jsonl) on every run that prices. Ships off (V2 s.7): Nick reads the picks for a week first, from Monday 11-16's window (python scripts\advice_show.py, the run summary), then turns it on -- an engine change: commit, push, set-engine.
advice._show_title_odds: true or false, required (anything else raises). Whether a pick's title-odds change is shown: the change in P(regular-season title) while the horizon starts in weeks 1-15, in P(champion) after. false (shipped 11-12): the hub's advice cards carry no title-odds number, and python scripts\advice_show.py prints "title odds: hidden". true: both show it. The ranking (the veto) uses the title term either way. The estimate tracks the season pass since the causal price of a point (claude/CAUSAL_LEVERAGE_RESULT_2026-11-12.md: held-out correlation 0.97, slope 1.01); turning it on is Nick's call -- an engine change: commit, push, set-engine.

payouts._comment: Manager-to-manager payments; the league keeps no pot. USD.

league_champion.paid_by: 3rd and 4th place in the regular-season standings (weeks 1-15)

playoff_champion.paid_by: 3rd and 4th place in the playoff bracket, as decided by the weeks 19-21 third-place series

cup_champion.prize: one more keeper than the other three, the FOLLOWING season (keeper_rules: 2027-28 on, the previous season's Cup winner keeps 6, everyone else 5). Zero dollars; the only result that changes next season's rules.

playoff_third_place.note: The weeks 19-21 third-place series. Pride only FOR NOW: both semifinal losers pay the playoff champion regardless. If a stake is ever added, set it here -- the code reads it, nothing is hard-coded.

cup_third_place.note: The week-23 game between the Cup semifinal losers. Played and recorded; no stake.

live_refresh._comment: Step 3b, tag freshness (claude/HANDOFF_STEP3B_TAG_FRESHNESS_2026-11-10.md). Every key is required: a missing one raises (scripts/run_guard.py, modules/nba_injury_report.py, modules/o_nudge.py). Times are the league clock (America/Los_Angeles) unless named otherwise.
live_refresh._afternoon_firings: The afternoon tag check's fixed daily firings (cron-job.org cannot follow a varying tip time). They MUST equal the cron-job.org 'Afternoon tags' job's times (deploy/state-repo/cron-job-org.json; tests/test_tag_freshness.py pins it). Chosen 11-10 from the season's real first tips (data/nba_schedule_2026-27.refetched.json): the only 3-firing set that covers 103 of the 116 non-window game days left (88.8%). The guard admits the firing in [first tip - afternoon_lead_minutes[1], first tip - afternoon_lead_minutes[0]], the latest if several; a day no firing covers is skipped and named in that night's run summary, never forced.
live_refresh._afternoon_days: The days the cron-job.org 'Afternoon tags' job fires (it must equal that job's days; tests pin it). Not Monday: a window Monday has the pre-tip runs, and a Monday that is not a window day (Mon 12-07, inside week 7's 14 days) is named SKIPPED in that night's summary.
live_refresh._firing_tolerance_minutes: How late a firing may land and still count as its scheduled slot (cron-job.org fires on time; GitHub's dispatch can lag a minute or two). Below the 15-minute spacing of the Monday firings, so one firing is never read as two slots.
live_refresh._monday_poll_slots: Monday window polling reuses the pre-tip job's every-15-minute firings: a firing whose slot minute is one of these, inside the window (12:01 AM to the last tip - 5 minutes) and outside the pre-tip window [first tip - 45 min, first tip), polls Yahoo's transactions. So at most one poll every 30 minutes.

nba_report._comment: The NBA's official injury report (Nick, 11-10: 'Out' counts as out for that game at once, and is flagged). Read by the nightly run, the afternoon check and Monday's pre-tip runs; every read is stored in output/nba_injury_reports.jsonl. index_url is per season: update it at the season reset. The PDF names carry the filing time on the NBA's clock (time_zone), in cadence_minutes steps; when the index cannot be read, the latest report is found by trying the last probe_steps filing times. A report older than stale_hours is not applied (named in the run summary). A missing or unreadable report never stops a run.

o_nudge._comment: The O-past-3-games nudge (run by the nightly only): a player tagged O who has missed more than more_than_games of his team's games, with no injury entry, gets one issue. Rostered players, and free agents with projected FPPG at or above free_agent_min_projected_fppg (the stash's candidates: since 48f an O with no entry is hidden from the stash). 26.0 is the builder's proposal, 11-10: the lowest projected FPPG on any roster that day (26.06), i.e. a free agent who would be rostered. Nick to confirm.
